newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends flat, month-end dlr demand low.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends flat, month-end dlr demand low.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Wednesday at 35.855/865 per dollar against the opening quotes of 35.86/87, dealers said.
A month-end spurt in dollar demand, which some dealers were expecting earlier this week, remained elusive, causing the rupee to end marginally up, some dealers said.
"There was some dollar demand but supplies were more than enough," a dealer said. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) which was active on Monday, had not bought dollars since, he said.
An executive at an engineering company said his bankers were advising customers not to cover their import liabilities given the rupee's stability in recent months.
Premia fluctuated in the forward market but some month-end paying pressure helped six-month annualised premium to end up at 7.20 percent compared to the previous close of 7.03 percent.
